details: Nasdaq has received conditional approval from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to list cash-settled Bitcoin index options. These European-style derivatives, trading under the ticker QBTC, will track the CME CF Bitcoin Real Time Index and settle in US dollars, eliminating the need for direct Bitcoin holdings. This development is seen as a further step towards institutional acceptance of cryptocurrencies.
title: Nasdaq Gains SEC Approval for Bitcoin Index Options

details: Bitcoin prices have been consolidating around the $77,000 mark after a volatile three-week correction. Sentiment has been influenced by speculation of a near-term US-Iran peace deal, which initially saw crypto prices edge higher. However, this positive sentiment is being counterbalanced by persistent institutional sell-offs and significant outflows from spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which shed over $1.25 billion in total investments recently. Overall, digital asset investment products experienced a net outflow of $1.47 billion last week, with Bitcoin seeing the largest weekly outflow in 2026 at $1.315 billion.
title: Bitcoin Consolidates Amid Geopolitical Hopes and ETF Outflows

details: Digital asset investment products recorded a substantial net outflow of $1.47 billion last week, marking the second consecutive week of negative growth and the third-largest weekly outflow for 2026. Bitcoin alone accounted for $1.315 billion of these outflows, which is the largest weekly outflow for the cryptocurrency this year. Ethereum also experienced outflows of $223 million. These outflows are closely linked to rising geopolitical risks.
title: Digital Asset Funds See Significant Outflows
